programme.name: BSc in Surveying

admission.title: Eligibility & Admission Criteria (DSE)
content: **Admission Score Formula**: Any Best 5 Subjects (plus 6th subject bonus).
**Average HKDSE Score with Subject Weighting**: 211.1 (2025 JUPAS data).
**Median Admission Score**: N/A (2025 JUPAS data).
**Lower Quartile**: N/A (2025 JUPAS data).
**Subject Weighting**: Subject weighting in details.
**Core Subjects Minimum Level**: Chinese Language 3, English Language 3, Mathematics (Compulsory Part) 2, Citizenship and Social Development Attained.
**Elective Subjects**: ANY 2 SUBJECTS at Level 3.
**Interview**: No interview required for standard JUPAS admission.
**Duration**: 4 years full-time.
**First Year Tuition**: HK$44,500 (local students).
**Note**: Subject weightings apply. See "Weightings" for details.

curriculum.title: Curriculum Overview
content: **Programme Overview**: JS3789 BSc in Surveying is a 4-year full-time programme under the Faculty of Construction and Environment, focusing on property and construction surveying with a strong emphasis on real estate development, valuation, and project management.

**Two Streams**: Students can choose between the Property and Construction Surveying stream or the General Practice Surveying stream, allowing specialisation in either technical construction or commercial property management.

**Year 1**: Foundation courses include Introduction to Surveying, Economics for Construction, Building Technology, and Mathematics for Surveyors, providing a solid grounding in both technical and business aspects.

**Year 2**: Core subjects such as Property Valuation, Land Law, Construction Technology, and Building Services Engineering are introduced, alongside the first Work-Integrated Education (WIE) placement opportunity.
**Year 3**: Advanced modules include Property Investment and Finance, Development Economics, Building Surveying, and Professional Practice, with a second WIE placement to build industry experience.

**Year 4**: Capstone project and electives like Urban Economics, Facility Management, and Real Estate Law, plus a final WIE placement or research dissertation, preparing students for professional accreditation.

career.title: Career Prospects
content: **Professional Accreditation**: Graduates are eligible for membership pathways with the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), Hong Kong Institute of Surveyors (HKIS), and other international bodies, enhancing global career mobility.
**Diverse Roles**: Career options include Chartered Surveyor, Property Valuer, Project Manager, Facilities Manager, and Development Consultant in both private and public sectors.

**Industry Demand**: Hong Kong's ongoing infrastructure projects and Greater Bay Area development create strong demand for surveying graduates, with starting salaries typically ranging from HKD 18,000 to 25,000 per month.
**Employer Network**: PolyU's strong ties with leading firms such as Swire Properties, Henderson Land, MTR Corporation, and the Hong Kong Housing Authority provide direct recruitment pipelines.

**Entrepreneurial Path**: Graduates can also establish their own surveying consultancy firms, leveraging the programme's business and legal training to serve property developers and government agencies.
**Further Studies**: Many graduates pursue master's degrees in Real Estate, Urban Planning, or Construction Law at top universities worldwide, including PolyU's own MSc in Real Estate.

campus.title: Campus Life & Facilities
content: **Prime Location**: PolyU is located in Hung Hom, Kowloon, directly connected to Hung Hom MTR station, providing easy access to Central, Tsim Sha Tsui, and the Greater Bay Area via high-speed rail.
**State-of-the-Art Labs**: The Faculty of Construction and Environment houses specialised surveying labs with 3D laser scanners, drones for aerial surveying, and GIS software for spatial analysis.
**Industry Simulation Centre**: A dedicated Surveying Studio simulates real-world property valuation and building inspection scenarios, allowing students to practice with professional-grade tools.
**Library Resources**: The Pao Yue-kong Library offers extensive databases for property research, including Land Registry records, valuation reports, and international surveying journals.
**Student Societies**: The PolyU Surveying Society organises site visits to major developments, networking events with industry professionals, and annual surveying competitions.
**Sports and Recreation**: The campus features a multi-purpose sports complex, swimming pool, and over 50 student clubs, ensuring a balanced university experience.

competitiveness.title: Competitiveness & Admission
content: **Overall Level**: High (★★★★☆)
**Admission Score Formula**: Any Best 5 Subjects with a 6th subject bonus, allowing students to maximise their score by including an extra elective.

**Subject Weighting**: Core subjects (English, Mathematics) and relevant electives (Economics, Geography, Physics, Design & Applied Technology) receive higher weighting, rewarding students with strong quantitative and analytical skills.
**Average HKDSE Score**: The average weighted score for 2025 admissions is 211.1, indicating a competitive threshold that requires solid performance across five subjects.
**Interview Requirement**: Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview, which assesses communication skills, problem-solving ability, and genuine interest in the surveying profession.

**Non-JUPAS Pathway**: The programme also accepts applicants with International Baccalaureate (IB), GCE A-Levels, or other equivalent qualifications, with competitive offers based on academic records and interviews.

alumni.title: Notable Alumni
content: **Dr. Thomas Tang (鄧智偉)**: Director of Lands, Hong Kong SAR Government. A leading figure in land administration and policy, graduated from PolyU's surveying programme in the 1990s.
**Mr. Vincent Ho (何志強)**: Managing Director, Savills Hong Kong. Oversees valuation and advisory services, recognised as a Fellow of RICS and HKIS.
**Ms. Karen Chan (陳嘉欣)**: Head of Property Development, MTR Corporation. Leads major rail-property integration projects, including the Lohas Park development.
**Mr. Alan Wong (黃偉倫)**: Founder and CEO, AWA Surveyors Limited. Established a successful surveying consultancy with over 100 staff, serving clients across Asia.
**Dr. Emily Lau (劉慧敏)**: Associate Professor, Department of Real Estate and Construction, University of Hong Kong. Published over 50 papers on urban economics and property valuation.
**Mr. Simon Lee (李志強)**: Senior Manager, Valuation and Advisory, CBRE Hong Kong. Specialises in complex valuation assignments for REITs and institutional investors.

scholarships.title: Scholarships & Financial Aid
content: **PolyU Entry Scholarship**: Awarded to top HKDSE scorers (e.g., 5** in multiple subjects) with a value of up to HKD 50,000 per year, renewable based on academic performance.

**Faculty of Construction and Environment Scholarship**: Offers HKD 20,000 to students with outstanding admission scores or exceptional performance in Year 1, with priority given to surveying programme students.
**Industry-Sponsored Awards**: Companies like Swire Properties and Henderson Land provide annual scholarships of HKD 15,000–30,000 for surveying students with strong academic and leadership records.
**HKIS Education Fund**: The Hong Kong Institute of Surveyors offers bursaries of up to HKD 40,000 for students demonstrating financial need and academic potential.
**Work-Integrated Education Stipend**: Students receive a stipend during WIE placements (typically HKD 8,000–12,000 per placement), helping offset living costs while gaining experience.

**Government Financial Assistance**: Eligible students can apply for the HKSAR Government's Grant and Loan Schemes, including the Tertiary Student Finance Scheme (TSFS) and Non-means-tested Loan Scheme (NLS).

tips.title: Ace Sir's JS3789 Strategy — 9 Actionable Tips
content: **1. Prioritise Core Subjects with Higher Weighting**
- Focus on English and Mathematics as they receive higher weighting in the admission formula. Aim for at least Level 4 in both, with Level 5 or above strongly recommended.
**2. Leverage the 6th Subject Bonus**
- Take an extra elective (e.g., Economics, Geography, or Physics) to boost your total score. A Level 4 in a 6th subject can add 10–15 points to your weighted average.
**3. Target a Weighted Score Above 220**
- With an average of 211.1, aim for a weighted score of 220+ to be competitive. Use PolyU's online score calculator to simulate your results with different subject combinations.
**4. Build a Strong Profile in Economics or Geography**
- These subjects are highly relevant to surveying. Achieving Level 5 or above in Economics or Geography signals strong analytical and spatial skills to the admissions panel.
**5. Prepare for the Interview with Real-World Cases**
- Research recent Hong Kong property developments (e.g., Kai Tak, Northern Metropolis) and practice discussing valuation or planning issues. Show genuine interest in the surveying profession.
**6. Gain Early Exposure Through Summer Programmes**
- Attend PolyU's summer workshops or industry talks organised by the Faculty of Construction and Environment. This demonstrates commitment and can strengthen your interview performance.
**7. Highlight Leadership and Teamwork in Your Application**
- Participate in school clubs, sports teams, or community projects. Surveying requires collaboration with architects, engineers, and clients, so evidence of teamwork is a plus.
**8. Explore Non-JUPAS Pathways if Needed**
- If your HKDSE results are borderline, consider retaking subjects or applying via International Baccalaureate (IB) or GCE A-Levels. The programme accepts multiple qualifications.
**9. Connect with Current Students and Alumni**
- Reach out to PolyU Surveying Society members on LinkedIn or attend open days. Insider advice on study tips, internship opportunities, and course selection can give you an edge.

admission.title: 入學要求與計分詳情 (DSE)
content: **入學計分公式**：任何最佳五科 (另加第6科加分)。
**文憑試成績平均積點（計算科目比重後）**：211.1（2025年聯招數據）。
**入學中位數**：N/A分（2025年聯招數據）。
**下四分位數**：N/A分（2025年聯招數據）。
**科目比重**：Subject weighting in details。
**核心科目最低要求**：中國語文第3級、英國語文第3級、數學（必修部分）第2級、公民與社會發展科達標。
**選修科目**：任何2科達第3級。
**面試**：標準聯招入學不需要面試。
**修讀年期**：4年全日制。
**首年學費**：港幣44,500元（本地學生）。
**備註**：科目比重詳見「比重」按鈕。

curriculum.title: 課程概覽
content: **課程概覽**：JS3789 地產及建設測量學(榮譽)理學士為四年全日制課程，隸屬於建設及環境學院，專注於房地產與建築測量，並強調物業發展、估值及項目管理。
**兩個專修**：學生可選擇「物業及建設測量」或「產業測量」分流，以便專注於技術性建築或商業物業管理。
**第一年**：基礎科目包括測量學導論、建築經濟學、建築技術及測量數學，為技術與商業層面打下穩固基礎。
**第二年**：核心科目如物業估值、土地法、建築技術及屋宇裝備工程陸續引入，並提供首次「工作整合教育」（WIE）實習機會。
**第三年**：進階單元包括物業投資與金融、發展經濟學、建築測量及專業實務，並進行第二次WIE實習以累積行業經驗。
**第四年**：畢業專題及選修科目如城市經濟學、設施管理及房地產法，加上最後一次WIE實習或研究論文，為專業認證做好準備。

career.title: 就業前景
content: **專業認證**：畢業生可申請英國皇家特許測量師學會（RICS）、香港測量師學會（HKIS）等國際機構的會員資格，提升全球職涯流動性。
**多元職位**：就業選擇包括特許測量師、物業估值師、項目經理、設施經理及發展顧問，涵蓋私營及公營機構。
**行業需求**：香港持續的基建項目及大灣區發展為測量畢業生創造強勁需求，起薪通常介乎每月港幣18,000至25,000元。
**僱主網絡**：理大與太古地產、恒基兆業、港鐵公司及香港房屋委員會等領先企業保持緊密聯繫，提供直接招聘渠道。
**創業路徑**：畢業生亦可創立個人測量顧問公司，運用課程的商業及法律訓練為物業發展商及政府機構提供服務。
**深造機會**：許多畢業生在全球頂尖大學攻讀房地產、城市規劃或建築法碩士學位，包括理大本身的房地產理學碩士課程。

campus.title: 校園生活與設施
content: **優越位置**：理大位於九龍紅磡，直接連接紅磡港鐵站，方便前往中環、尖沙咀及經高鐵通往大灣區。
**先進實驗室**：建設及環境學院設有專業測量實驗室，配備3D激光掃描儀、航拍測量無人機及地理信息系統軟件。
**行業模擬中心**：專屬測量工作室模擬真實物業估值及建築檢測場景，讓學生使用專業級工具進行練習。
**圖書館資源**：包玉剛圖書館提供豐富的物業研究數據庫，包括土地註冊紀錄、估值報告及國際測量期刊。
**學生學會**：理大測量學會組織大型發展項目實地考察、業界專業人士交流活動及年度測量比賽。
**體育與康樂**：校園設有多用途體育綜合大樓、游泳池及超過50個學生社團，確保均衡的大學體驗。

competitiveness.title: 競爭力與入學要求
content: **入學分數公式**：最佳5科成績，並設有第6科加分機制，讓學生透過額外選修科提升總分。
**科目比重**：核心科目（英文、數學）及相關選修科（經濟、地理、物理、設計與應用科技）獲較高比重，獎勵數理及分析能力強的學生。
**平均文憑試分數**：2025年入學的加權平均分為211.1分，顯示需要五科穩定表現才能達到競爭門檻。
**面試要求**：獲篩選的申請人可能獲邀面試，評估溝通能力、解難技巧及對測量專業的熱誠。
**非聯招途徑**：課程亦接受國際文憑（IB）、GCE A-Level或其他同等學歷的申請人，根據學術成績及面試發出競爭性取錄。

alumni.title: 知名校友
content: **鄧智偉博士**：香港特別行政區政府地政總署署長，土地行政與政策領域的領袖人物，1990年代畢業於理大測量課程。
**何志強先生**：第一太平戴維斯香港董事總經理，負責估值及顧問服務，獲評為RICS及HKIS資深會員。
**陳嘉欣女士**：港鐵公司物業發展主管，領導多個鐵路加物業綜合項目，包括日出康城發展。
**黃偉倫先生**：AWA測量師有限公司創辦人及行政總裁，成功創立擁有超過100名員工的測量顧問公司，服務亞洲客戶。
**劉慧敏博士**：香港大學房地產及建設系副教授，發表超過50篇關於城市經濟學及物業估值的學術論文。
**李志強先生**：世邦魏理仕香港估值及顧問部高級經理，專注於房地產投資信託基金及機構投資者的複雜估值項目。

scholarships.title: 獎學金與資助
content: **理大入學獎學金**：頒予文憑試成績優異者（如多科5**），每年最高港幣50,000元，可按學業成績續領。
**建設及環境學院獎學金**：提供港幣20,000元予入學分數突出或一年級表現卓越的學生，測量課程學生獲優先考慮。
**行業贊助獎項**：太古地產及恒基兆業等公司每年提供港幣15,000至30,000元獎學金，獎勵學業及領導力出色的測量學生。
**香港測量師學會教育基金**：香港測量師學會提供最高港幣40,000元的助學金，支援有經濟需要及學術潛力的學生。
**工作整合教育津貼**：學生在WIE實習期間可獲津貼（通常每次實習港幣8,000至12,000元），幫助減輕生活開支。
**政府資助計劃**：合資格學生可申請香港特區政府的資助及貸款計劃，包括專上學生資助計劃（TSFS）及免入息審查貸款計劃（NLS）。

tips.title: Ace Sir JS3789 攻略 — 9 個實用貼士
content: **1. 優先處理比重較高的核心科目**
- 集中提升英文及數學成績，因為它們在入學公式中佔較高比重。目標至少達到第4級，強烈建議第5級或以上。
**2. 善用第6科加分機制**
- 選修額外科目（如經濟、地理或物理）以提高總分。第6科取得第4級可為加權平均分增加10至15分。
**3. 目標加權分數達220分以上**
- 鑑於平均分為211.1分，目標加權分數應達220分或以上以保持競爭力。使用理大網上分數計算器模擬不同科目組合的結果。
**4. 在經濟或地理科建立優勢**
- 這些科目與測量高度相關。在經濟或地理科取得第5級或以上，可向入學委員會展示出色的分析及空間能力。
**5. 以真實案例準備面試**
- 研究近期香港物業發展項目（如啟德、北部都會區），並練習討論估值或規劃議題。展現對測量專業的熱誠。
**6. 透過暑期課程提早接觸行業**
- 參加理大建設及環境學院舉辦的暑期工作坊或行業講座。這可展示你的投入程度，並有助提升面試表現。
**7. 在申請中突出領導力與團隊合作**
- 參與學校學會、運動隊伍或社區項目。測量工作需要與建築師、工程師及客戶協作，團隊合作經驗是加分項。
**8. 如有需要，探索非聯招途徑**
- 如果文憑試成績處於邊緣，可考慮重考科目或透過國際文憑（IB）或GCE A-Level申請。課程接受多種學歷。
**9. 與現屆學生及校友建立聯繫**
- 在LinkedIn上聯絡理大測量學會成員，或參加開放日。有關學習貼士、實習機會及選科建議的內部資訊可讓你佔優。
